title: JWT clock drift & intermittent 429 tinkering log
content:
Summary:
Tried to reproduce recurring burst 429s correlated with new short-lived JWTs issued by the auth proxy. Hypothesis: client clock drift causes tokens to be considered not-yet-valid (nbf) or triggers small windows where multiple clients re-request tokens simultaneously, creating a thundering herd that trips per-key rate quotas. Notes below are an exploratory solo playbook: commands, raw errors, telemetry, and quick experiments.

Observed behavior (field):
- Multiple services report transient 429 on Redwood API routes for the same API key around midnight UTC (roughly).
- Some 401s co-occur but are temporally distinct in logs (different services).
- Rate-limit headers inconsistent: sometimes X-RateLimit-Remaining present, sometimes absent.
- A subset of clients are using short TTL JWTs (1m–5m) minted by our proxy. Suspect simultaneous refreshes.

Immediate reproduction attempts (local):
1) Issue a short-lived JWT locally (via auth-proxy):
- Command: curl -s -X POST "https://auth-proxy.local/issue" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"sub":"svc-test","ttl":60}'
- Response: {"jwt":"eyJhbGciOi...","expires_in":60}

2) Call Redwood endpoint with that JWT in Authorization header repeatedly in a tight loop to see rate headers:
- for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'; done
- Observed: first ~50 calls return 200 with X-RateLimit-Remaining decrementing; around the 60th–80th call some responses become 429 with no consistent Retry-After header.

3) Simulate clock skew by shifting local system clock forward/back:
- sudo date -s "+15 seconds" (and +60s) while replaying calls above.
- Result: when client clock ahead by ~30–90s, first few calls get 401 (token not valid yet) or 401-like signatures; then server accepts after small delay.
- When many clients had clock drift forward, we see repeated token re-issue attempts and a spike in auth-proxy requests.

Server-side traces and logs (abridged):
- auth-proxy logs (INFO): token-issue request rate jumped 7x at 00:01:02 UTC.
- gateway logs: 429 bursts with correlation ids. Example line:
  ts=2025-01-11T00:01:03Z level=warn route=/v1/generate status=429 api_key=acct_XXXXX req_id=req-9a4b
- gateway debug: upstream_auth_check failed: token nbf in future (client clock  +40s). Recorded as auth-fail then retry.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Clock drift causes clients to fail token validation locally or at gateway; they re-request tokens en masse -> auth-proxy throttling -> downstream 429s.
B) Short TTL tokens lead to synchronized refreshes (token stampede) when many instances start at same time (cron jobs / deployments).
C) Rate-limit enforcement bug: some code path decrements quota even on auth failures, causing tokens to lose remaining quota unexpectedly.
D) Caching/edge misconfiguration: inconsistent propagation of X-RateLimit headers and missing Retry-After could be due to async response path.

Quick experiments performed and outcomes:
- Increase TTL to 10m for test clients: burst 429 frequency dropped by ~60% in local repro. Suggests refresh timing contributes.
- Add jitter to refresh schedule (random 0–30s): nearly eliminated test-thundering.
- Forced client clock skew in a cluster of 30 replicas: observed auth-proxy QPS spike and ~20% 429s.
- Instrumented auth-proxy to log token-issuers per second: confirmed that during incidents, token-issue rate correlates with 429 spike.

Commands and snippets used (copyable):
- Issue JWT (test):
  JWT=$(curl -s -X POST "https://auth-proxy.local/issue" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"sub":"svc-test","ttl":60}' | jq -r .jwt)
- Hit endpoint in loop with basic timing:
  for i in {1..200}; do t=$(date +%s%3N); curl -s -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"; done
- Dump gateway headers (first successful then 429):
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" | sed -n '1,40p'

Debugging checklist for next steps: 
- [ ] Correlate incident timestamps with NTP/chrony logs for affected hosts (client-side).
- [ ] Add server-side metric: token-issue-rate per API key and per service to detect stampedes earlier.
- [ ] Ensure gateway does not decrement quota on auth validation failures (audit code path).
- [ ] Return consistent Retry-After + standard X-RateLimit headers on 429s.
- [ ] Prototype sticky jittering in auth-proxy (randomized refresh window per instance).

Notes-to-self / gotchas: 
- Some customers run hosts in environments with bad NTP (cellular edges) — ex: client reported +2m drift last year.
- Be cautious: increasing TTL reduces auth security surface; prefer jitter + small TTLs rather than long TTLs.
- Watch per-key quota semantics for dedicated vs hosted customers (different buckets).

Outstanding questions to bring to infra sync:
- Can we surface a signal in Console for token-issue-rate spikes per key? (ops ask)
- Is there an internal knob to treat auth-failures as non-decrementing for rate windows?
- Should we enforce server-side acceptance window (leeway) for nbf/iat to absorb small skews? Pros/cons?

Related artifacts (quick list):
- INF JIRA: INF-4372 (token-stampede investigation)
- PR: runtime/#6123 (add token-issue metrics)
- Slack thread: #infra-auth (pinned: thread around 2024-12-30)

Short-term mitigation (recommended):
1) Deploy auth-proxy change to add small random jitter [0-30s] to token refresh scheduling for services that use automatic renew.
2) Add 30s leeway for nbf/iat checks on gateway validation to tolerate minor client drift.
3) Instrument and alert on token-issue-rate anomalies (threshold: 5x baseline for 1m window).

If I get time this week: collect per-key example logs and build a small viz (timeseries) showing token-issue events vs 429 spikes; add to INF-4372 for postmortem.

Raw error excerpts captured during repro (copied):
---
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Sat, 11 Jan 2025 00:01:04 GMT
X-Request-ID: req-9a4b
Content-Length: 0
---
---
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Sat, 11 Jan 2025 00:01:02 GMT
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Token not valid yet (nbf)"
X-Request-ID: req-9a2f
---

End of notes.
